scores.evidence_span: VietnamOnline recommends avoiding strenuous outdoor activity around 11:00–14:00 and using beaches before about 09:30 or from late afternoon [3]. This schedule is especially appropriate with a five-year-old.
scores.rationale: An identifiable source provides time-specific evidence for evaluating a comfortable schedule with a midday activity break.

scores.evidence_span: Shanghai and Bali are both UTC+8, so no clock-change jet lag is expected. Travel fatigue still warrants a light first day.
scores.rationale: Provides a verifiable destination-specific time-zone fact and explicitly connects it to travel fatigue and pacing.

scores.evidence_span: do not replace this with a Nusa Penida speedboat day. The boat journey, sea variability, road conditions and long excursion structure are poor matches for a restful trip with a five-year-old.
scores.rationale: Names a contrasting excursion and identifies boat travel and a long excursion structure as concrete burdens. Its tightly packed character is less fully established because no duration or sightseeing sequence is supplied.

scores.evidence_span: For Bali, the best-value version is not the cheapest room or the busiest itinerary. It is a **two-bedroom Sanur base, direct flights if affordable, two paid family attractions, two slow beach/pool days, one flexible weather day and protected midday rest every day**.
scores.rationale: Directly contrasts the busiest itinerary with a specifically allocated restful plan on a best-value axis, although the consequential disadvantages of the busy alternative are not developed in this comparison.

scores.evidence_span: Sanur is preferable to Kuta for this family because it is quieter, easier to walk, less focused on nightlife and has a calmer shoreline.
scores.rationale: Explicitly selects a named destination over another because of characteristics supporting comfort and lower-effort days.
